chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Ibn Othayna, from Ma'roof ibn Kharrabooth, who said:
Whenever we entered upon Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), he would not fail to say: 'Khurasan, Khurasan; Sajistan, Sajistan,' as if he were giving us good news with that.

key_terms.خُرَاسَانُ: Khurasan (a historical region in Northeast Iran/Afghanistan/Central Asia)
key_terms.سِجِسْتَانُ: Sajistan (a historical region in Southeast Iran/Southwest Afghanistan)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Khurasan and Sajistan in Shia eschatology according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In the Book of Ghayba, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) repeatedly emphasized Khurasan and Sajistan, signaling their pivotal role in the eschatological narrative of the Mahdi's (peace be upon him) rise. This specific repetition highlights these eastern regions as the primary launchpad for the initial uprising (Qiyam) that precedes the global establishment of justice, a theme deeply rooted in Shia hadith literature regarding the signs of the Occultation.
